BiblicalUsage: To strip off is the word for plucking ears and cropping twigs: when thou comest into the standing corn of thy neighbour, thou mayest pluck the ears with thine hand; the eagle cropped off the top of his young twigs; and the outcasts cut up mallows by the bushes for their meat.
TheologicalSignificance: I read the stripping as the small taking that the law allows and the hunger that drives men to the bushes.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
